title: Drift Correction
hook: Nobody decides to get sloppy. Standards just slide a little every week until you finally notice.
statement: Everything drifts away from the standard over time. You have to pull it back on purpose, regularly.
explainer: Response times creep up, quality slips, discounts get handed out. Small corrections done often are way easier than one big cleanup after things fall apart.
sop: Write down the original standard for one key process.
Rate how far you've drifted from it right now, 1 to 10.
Set your Frequency. Weekly for fast-moving areas, monthly for slower ones.
At every check, pull it back toward standard and rate the Gap Closed.
If drift keeps growing, raise your Frequency.
equation_example: Each fix closes the gap by about 6 out of 10, and you correct 4 times a month. Gap Closed 6 × Frequency 4 = 24. Higher means you're catching drift as it happens. Lower means it's piling up faster than you fix it.
question: Write down your weekly reset ritual. If you don't have one, write the day you'll start.
closing_statement: A standard you never re-check is already slipping.
caption:
Principle Nº 148: Drift Correction

Nobody decides to get sloppy. Standards just slide a little every week until you finally notice.

Everything drifts away from the standard over time. You have to pull it back on purpose, regularly.

Your turn: Write down your weekly reset ritual. If you don't have one, write the day you'll start.
